subject: Use camtrapR for tables of previously identified images

messages.author: da3fd983e2dbcaff
messages.subject: Use camtrapR for tables of previously identified images
parts:
Excellent work with the camtrapR package! 

In reading through the vignettes, it seems like the package is designed to manage the entire workflow from image identification through analysis. Is it possible to import tables of previously identified images rather than using raw camera images? We have been using the Wild.ID format for our camera images, and I'd like to use these data in camtrapR. If you can provide any advice on where to jump into the camtrapR workflow, I'd appreciate it.

messages.author: 9c3183af58028473
messages.subject: Re: Use camtrapR for tables of previously identified images
parts:
Yes - it is simple.  Have a look at the structure of the stations and the species tables in camtrapR.  

Organise your data into the same format - you will likely do this in excel and export as a csv or text file. The camtrapR fields will be needed but any extra fields can come in too.  The dates will be  a hassle.  Don't be too clever and don't use tidy verse and a tibble, stick with base R data frames.

Read the two tables (as data frames) into camtrapR.

The rest of camtrapR functions will all work for organising, reporting, analysing and plotting.

I brought my 350 stations and 400 000 image records into camtrapR this way.  I had used exifPro where you used Wild.ID.  We had to do much cleaning of the data (getting the stations names and the species names, date formats completely consistent) but you probably have that all tidy.

We have considerable R script - if you need it.

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Use camtrapR for tables of previously identified images
parts:
Hi,
as David said, it is easy to use camtrapR on existing datasets.. The minimum requirements are are two data frames with the following information:

camera trap table:
- station name/id
- setup + retrieval dates
- coordinates (for detectionMaps and creating capthist objects with spatialDetectionHistory)

record table:
- station name/id (matching camera trap table)
- species name
- date + time of records


All other fields are optional. You don't need directory, filename and the deltatime fields for running camtrapR. You don't even need the images once your record table is done. Please note that currently there is no function to filter for temporal independence in an existing record table. The filter is built into the recordTable function.
See data(camtraps) and data(recordTableSample) for examples.
Best regards,
Jürgen
